links.comparator_used: Classical OOD detection methods (widely known baselines), compared across four dataset shifts
links.outcome: Detection of near- and far-OOD samples across four dataset shifts for a lung nodule malignancy DL model
links.effect: Mahalanobis distance method outperformed the classical methods and detected near- and far-OOD samples across all datasets; no numeric values given in the abstract. It could also incorporate additional ID data while still distinguishing the remaining OOD cases.
links.tradeoff: No decline in DL model performance was found as the OOD score increased, so an optimal OOD threshold at which performance stays reliable could not be identified.
links.quote: The results show that our proposed method outperforms the classical methods and can effectively detect near- and far-OOD samples across all datasets with different data distribution shifts.

design_hint: out-of-distribution detection as a safeguard added to an existing model
